ev.q: Twelve of 13 ill persons reported UPMIW exposure in city A during the week before symptom onset
STEC O157:H7 was isolated from UPMIW reservoir sediment and dead-end ultrafiltration water samples from five of nine exposure sites.
Twelve of 13 ill persons reported UPMIW exposure in city A during the week before symptom onset
with illness onsets during July 22–August 31 ( Figure 1 )
Seven patients were hospitalized, including two with HUS; no deaths were reported.
two exposure sites with detectable STEC O157:H7 had no detectable coliforms or generic E. coli
Local, state, and federal public health partners investigating the outbreak linked the illnesses to untreated, pressurized, municipal irrigation water (UPMIW) exposure in city A

methods_quotes.q: Grab water samples were tested for generic E. coli and total coliforms per 100 mL.
Microbial source tracking was performed for all dead-end ultrafiltration samples and both reservoir sediment samples
Of 12 samples analyzed by microbial source tracking (10 dead-end ultrafiltration and two sediment)
WGS results indicated clinical isolates were within 0–1 allele difference of each other
Among seven ill persons with discrete UPMIW exposure dates, the median incubation period was 3 days (range = 1–5 days).
